metadata.summary: Manchester City have signed Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea for a joint-British-record fee of £125m.
metadata.content: Enzo Fernandez transfer news: Man City sign midfielder from Chelsea in British-record-equalling £125m deal | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Enzo Fernandez transfer news: Man City sign midfielder from Chelsea in British-record-equalling £125m deal Enzo Fernandez joins Man City from Chelsea for £125m; Fee matches British record Liverpool paid Newcastle for Alexander Isak last summer; Chelsea furious that Monaco pulled out of deal to sell Lamine Camara as replacement for Fernandez Wednesday 2 September 2026 00:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher believes the signing of Enzo Fernandez will make Man City Arsenal's biggest title challenger Manchester City have signed Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea for a joint-British-record fee of £125m. The size of the fee matches the amount Liverpool paid Newcastle for Alexander Isak on Deadline Day a year ago. The Argentine midfielder has signed a five-year deal at the Etihad Stadium. The Fernandez deal comes amid Chelsea fury that Monaco pulled out of selling Lamine Camara - who was deemed as the Argentine's replacement - in the final minutes of the window. Chelsea had the option of pulling the plug on Fernandez to Man City after the Camara deal collapsed - but they stuck to their word and honoured their commitment to complete the deal. metadata.summary: Arthur Fery's hopes of a fairy-tale debut run at the US Open were ended in the first round by a straight-sets defeat to Lorenzo Musetti at Flushing Meadows.
metadata.content: US Open 2026: Arthur Fery beaten by Lorenzo Musetti in straight sets on Flushing Meadows debut | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open 2026: Arthur Fery beaten by Lorenzo Musetti in straight sets on Flushing Meadows debut Arthur Fery's US Open debut ends in first-round defeat to Lorenzo Musetti; British No 1's hopes of another Grand Slam fairy tale after Wimbledon dashed in straight-sets loss; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app Jack Wilkinson Sports Journalist @jacktwilkinson Wednesday 2 September 2026 00:52, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Arthur Fery against Lorenzo Musetti from the US Open. Arthur Fery's hopes of a fairy-tale debut run at the US Open were ended in the first round by a straight-sets defeat to Lorenzo Musetti at Flushing Meadows. One week on from reaching the final of the Winston-Salem Open, Fery's hopes to replicating his magical run to the Wimbledon semi-finals were dashed in a clinical 6-3 6-3 7-5 defeat to the 13th seed. Fery was crucially broken in the eighth game of the first set as back-to-back double faults gifted the initiative to Musetti, who broke serve again to wrap up the opener 6-3. Premier League clubs spent more on players than in any transfer window in the sport's history. City's spending reached £440m but they brought in £315m. Chelsea spent £342m and brought in even more. Money flowing in and out at unprecedented levels. Fernandez embodies the escalation in microcosm. Three-and-a-half years ago, his signing for £106.8m was held up as an example of excess. Tuesday 1 September 2026 23:24, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Stoke and Norwich. Ethan Galbraith earned Stoke their first points of the Championship season with a 1-0 victory over Norwich at the bet365 Stadium. The Potters had lost all three of their opening league games, including Saturday's 4-1 loss at Wolves, conceding nine goals in the process. Stoke had only won three times in the league since Norwich's 1-0 victory at the bet365 on January 4, a run of 23 games. After picking up their first win of the season with an impressive 4-1 victory over Burnley on Saturday, Norwich were condemned to their third defeat in four matches, leaving them also with just three points.
